item.title: Site-Specific Speciation of Vanadium Sites on γ-Al2O3 Facets and Edges from 51V SSNMR Spectroscopy
item.description:
γ-alumina (γ-Al2O3) supported vanadium oxide represent a notable class of heterogenous catalysts used for the direct oxidative propane dehydrogenation (ODH) reaction. However, while the presence of highly dispersed VOx (V5+) species has been established, understanding the exact structure of surface sites and the role of supports remains a pivotal objective for establishing structure-property relationships. Considering the structural complexity of γ-Al2O3 surfaces, where distinct surface sites emerge as a function of specific facets and edges, clarifying how the support dictates vanadium speciation remains a key objective. In this work, we employ Surface Organometallic Chemistry (SOMC) approach to evaluate the impact of the γ-Al2O3 nanocrystals morphology on the nature and structure of surface vanadium sites. Specifically, we grafted vanadyl isopropoxide (VO(OiPr)3) on tailored γ-Al2O3 nanocrystals, namely Rhomboids, Laths and Needles, exposing varying distributions of (110), (100) and (111) facets along with characteristic edges sites. Subsequent calcination yields supported, organic-ligand-free, monomeric vanadia sites. Advanced 51V solid-state NMR spectroscopy combined with DFT calculations reveals that grafting on γ-Al2O3 partially dehydroxylated at 500 °C directly generate bipodal VO(OiPr) species, whose structures depend on the underlying surface facets and edge sites. Furthermore, the supported vanadia sites formed upon calcination are also characterized by distinct V-O coordination numbers and hydroxylation states, which are quantitatively resolved across γ-Al2O3 morphologies. This work not only elucidates the complex speciation of V supported on γ-Al2O3 support, but also offers fundamental insights into the reactive surface sites on γ-Al2O3 that stabilize isolated metal species.

Weicheng Cao, Charles Sidhoum, Andri Florin, Christophe Copéret

item.title: OptiMatLLM: A Benchmark Suite and a Lightweight Domain-Specific LLM for Optical Materials Research
item.description:
The design of optical materials relies on highly specialized knowledge, which creates a major bottleneck for data-driven scientific discovery in the optical material domain. Large language models open new possibilities for scientific research, but general-purpose models struggle with the domainspecific physical logic and terminology. More importantly, no standardized evaluation benchmark exists to systematically assess how well LLMs perform on optical materials tasks. To fill this gap, we first construct two evaluation benchmarks, Optic_Choice and Optic_QA, designed specifically for the optical materials domain. We build a high-quality instruction-tuning dataset of 23,225 question-answer pairs through an automated multi-stage pipeline from a curated corpus of papers and textbook. We then develop OptiMatLLM, a 7-billion-parameter LLM fine-tuned LLM on this corpus. Evaluation results show that OptiMatLLM achieves top performance on our optical benchmarks, reaching 0.79 accuracy on Optic_Choice, while also performing competitively on broader scientific tests such as CMHChem, ChemBench, and MaScQA. The model retains strong general capabilities as well, scoring 0.91 on the GSM8K mathematical reasoning benchmark. We further provide a systematic comparison of multiple leading models on these benchmarks, establishing a reference for future work. All benchmarks, dataset, and model are publicly released to support further research on LLMs for optical and optoelectronic materials design.

Xinyi Wang, Youle Wang, Lei Zhang

item.title: Linear-response TDDFT simulations of K-edge resonant inelastic X-ray scattering in extended systems
item.description:
We present an implementation for the calculation of K-edge resonant inelastic X-ray scattering spectra based on time-dependent density functional theory in the CP2K package. The method evaluates the Kramers-Heisenberg cross section from transition dipole moments connecting the ground state, core-excited intermediate states, and valence-excited final states. The present implementation combines the existing linear response time-dependent density functional theory modules (XAS-TDP and TDDFT) within a unified framework. The resulting approach is computationally efficient and well suited for condensed-phase applications in combination with ab initio molecular dynamics. The implementation is validated against experiment and established reference calculations for gas-phase water and methanol at the oxygen K-edge. Its applicability to realistic condensed-phase systems is then demonstrated for crystalline kaolinite at the oxygen K-edge, and for aqueous ammonia at the nitrogen K-edge, where representative configurations are sampled from ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories.

Beliz Sertcan Gökmen, Michael R. Coates, Jürg Hutter, Marcella Iannuzzi

item.title: Dynamic Evolution and Stability of Ketenes in MAPO-18 (M = Si or Mg): Molecular Insights into the Reaction Mechanism for CO2-to-Hydrocarbons
item.description:
AEI topology molecular sieves (MAPO-18) have shown promising properties as components of OX-ZEO type tandem catalysts, where the Brønsted acid sites (BAS) introduced by different framework substitutions lead to distinct catalytic mechanisms on the CO2-to-hydrocarbons conversion. Ketenes are key intermediates in the conversion of methanol to hydrocarbons. This study provides molecular-level insights into the reactions of three ketenes (ketene, methyl ketene, and dimethyl ketene) with the BAS in MAPO-18 (M = Si, Mg) molecular sieves at operando conditions through first-principles molecular dynamics (FPMD) simulations combined with enhanced sampling techniques. Free energy surfaces constructed from FPMD simulations revealed distinct kinetic and thermodynamic preferences, linking them to different reaction routes for the production of olefins. Prior studies suggested that ketenes and their protonated analogues are key intermediates in two different pathways to olefins formation, and the three ketenes exhibited higher kinetic stability than their protonated forms in H-SAPO-18 compared to H-MgAPO-18, suggesting a high tendency for olefin production via the (cyclo)addition-decarboxylation route in H-SAPO-18. In contrast, the increased stability of the cationic intermediates and low protonation barrier for methyl and dimethyl ketenes in MgAPO-18 favor their direct decarbonylation to olefins. Surface-bound species displayed decreasing stability from surface acetate to surface propionate to surface isobutyrate , aligning with established trends for surface alkoxides. Moreover, a comparison with static calculations demonstrates their limited ability to capture the entropic contributions and dynamic effects that dominate the behavior of active intermediates under realistic reaction conditions, highlighting the necessity of molecular dynamics (MD) approaches for accurate mechanistic modeling of catalytic reactions. Benchmarking against high-level random phase approximation (RPA) calculations further revealed that the density functional theory (DFT) method in combination with the revPBE-D3 functional used in the FPMD simulations may overestimate the stability of cationic intermediates and underestimate the protonation barriers of ketene. Together, these findings underscore the importance of combining dynamic simulations with accurate potential energy descriptions to reliably model active intermediates in confined microporous environments. Overall, this study provides key steps of ketene reactivity in zeolite frameworks, bridging computational and experimental insights into CO2-to-hydrocarbon conversion pathways. These results emphasize how subtle variations in the framework composition and substituents dictate the reaction mechanisms, offering guidance for the rational design of molecular sieves tailored for selective catalytic transformations.

Wei Chen, Massimo Bocus, Unni Olsbye, Veronique Van Speybroeck

item.title: First-principles Investigation of Reconstructions for the Polar CoO (111) Surface and the Impact on Nanoparticle Morphology
item.description:
Reconstructions of the polar CoO (111) surface defines critical properties that impacts application in catalysis, energy storage and electrochemistry. However, these surface reconstructions are relatively unexplored, compared to its isomorphic analogues, and greater understanding of CoO surfaces is needed to enable rational control of surface stability and reactivity. We investigate the surface reconstructions of the polar (111) facet of rocksalt CoO in equilibrium with an oxygen environment using first principles calculations in conjunction with surface thermodynamics. Surface reconstruction, which can expose high-index facets has received limited attention despite experimental evidence. Therefore, we have additionally considered high-index facets in our calculations to obtain a comprehensive understanding of CoO surfaces. Our results demonstrate that high-index facets, such as (331) and (311), are more stable than the oxygen terminated (111) surface and low-index (100) and (110) surfaces across a range of meaningful oxygen chemical potentials. The stability of the highindex surfaces is identified to be due to the crystal structure and strong interaction between the oxygen and cobalt atoms of the open high-index surfaces. Our results on stability of high-index facets shows that surface roughening could offer a mechanism to compensate the polarity of (111) surface. Polarity compensation mechanisms allow the occurrence of polar surfaces in experiments. Our work offers new insights into the stability of polar rocksalt CoO surfaces and provides a foundation for understanding and tuning the properties that govern its performance in catalysis, energy storage, and electrochemical applications.

Akash Hiregange, Pavel V. Stishenko, Sarah J. Haigh, James Paterson, Mark Peacock, Andrew J. Logsdail

item.title: Unveiling Surface Reaction Networks in Biomass-Derived Compound Upgrading
item.description:
Biomass-derived platform molecules often undergo complex surface reactions in which productive routes compete with catalyst deactivation, limiting catalyst selectivity and stability. Identifying the molecular origins of these competing processes remains challenging, as conventional computational approaches generally rely on chemical intuition and hypothesis-driven rules, while strongly adsorbed intermediates and poisoning species remain difficult to characterize experimentally. Here, we combine enhanced sampling reaction discovery techniques with machine learning interatomic potentials, experimental catalytic tests, and in situ DRIFTS to unravel the surface reaction network controlling methyl levulinate conversion on zirconia. Our simulations reveal a highly interconnected network of elementary transformations in which surface Lewis acidic Zr sites and basic oxides cooperatively promote carbonyl activation and α-deprotonation, giving rise to competing pathways toward cyclization and catalyst poisoning. This mechanistic picture is supported by experimental evidence, which reveal a progressive decrease in angelica-lactone formation and the accumulation of persistent carboxylate-like surface species. Our results show that the same cooperative acid base surface motif which activates the substrate and promotes productive cyclization, also induces irreversible surface trapping leading to catalyst poisoning. By revealing this intrinsic competition at the molecular level, our work provides a clue on how to steer zirconia reactivity toward selective biomass conversion while suppressing the formation of the persistent surface species responsible for deactivation. More broadly, our work establishes a general strategy to tackle complex reaction networks in heterogeneous catalysis.

Fabio Loprete, Axel Tosello Gardini, Luca Visentin, Umberto Raucci, Lorenzo Mauro, Riccardo Tarroni, Fabrizio Cavani, Tommaso Tabanelli, Ivan Rivalta, Michele Parrinello

item.title: OptoMatKG: A Traceable Knowledge Graph Framework with Semantic Retrieval for Optoelectronic Materials Science
item.description:
Extracting and correlating knowledge from heterogeneous scientific publications poses a fundamental data engineering challenge for data-driven materials discovery. Traditional keyword search lacks semantic depth, while generic large language models (LLMs) are prone to hallucinated predictions. To address these limitations, we present OptoMatKG, a literature-scale data engineering system whose core contributions are threefold: (1) a domain-specific knowledge graph construction pipeline based on a nine-category fullworkflow ontology; the resulting graph comprises 2.62 million entities and 3.38 million typed relations; (2) a cascaded multi-stage retrieval pipeline that synergistically integrates LLM-based query normalization, semantic vector indexing and Materials Project pre-filtering to enhance metric-aware candidate ranking; and (3) an evidence-constrained auditing module that forces every output to anchor to DOI-supported reasoning chains, thereby enforcing end-to-end hallucination prevention. Using optoelectronic inverse design as a validation testbed, experiments verify that our entity extractor reaches a micro-averaged F1 of 0.971. Comprehensive tests over 2000 real-world queries further demonstrate that our system surpasses keyword-based and singlestage baselines in Recall@K and metric coverage. The system accurately quantifies multi-objective performance trade-offs while ensuring fully traceable inference. Although validated on photodetectors, the proposed solution provides a generalizable, pluggable engineering framework readily extendable to other functional material discovery pipelines.

Ben Ni, Lei Zhang

item.title: Open Sesame! Simulation of the Adsorption Induced Phase Transformation Mechanism of MOF Nanocrystallites
item.description:
One of the most compelling features of certain MOFs is their ability to undergo stimuli-induced phase transformations with large changes in the accessible pore volume, leading to phenomena like “gate opening”. Theoretical simulations are an indispensable tool in order to understand such processes on a molecular level. However, adsorption phenomena are usually investigated within the approximation of periodic boundary conditions (PBC) and using Grand Canonical methods. This ignores the interface to the gas reservoir and any transport effects, which prevents the investigation of transformation kinetics. Previously, we developed methods to simulate explicit MOF nanocrystallites beyond PBC with the aim to understand size effects. In this work, the results of the natural next step, namely an in silico adsorption experiment for DUT-8 (Cu) nanocrystallites (about 10 nm edge length) in a reservoir of carbon dioxide are presented: Unbiased molecular dynamics simulations reveal a surprisingly rapid gate opening within a few nanoseconds. The first-order phase transition is initiated by a characteristic pore opening at an edge of the crystallite. The anisotropy of the pillared-layer MOF, with its channels along the crystallographic c-axis, leads to a rapid transport along these channels when the pore opening of the MOF proceeds. The simulations allow for an unprecedented view on the molecular mechanism, including the structural transformation of the MOF and the connected transport of the guest molecules into the MOF pores. Already this first attempt of a realistic adsorption simulation beyond PBC revealed the widening of a single channel at the obtuse angle edge of the NC as the secret “Open Sesame!” to open the gate. This confirms that for an in–depth view into the kinetics of adsorption induced phase transformations, an explicit interface between MOF and gas reservoir is pivotal and serves as a basis for further investigations with even larger systems and more realistic surface terminations to be performed in the future.

Rochus Schmid, Larissa Schaper

item.title: Nonequilibrium Electronic Response Modes Govern Catalytic Energetics under Illumination
item.description:
While nonequilibrium electronic configurations generated under illumination are widely recognized as central to photocatalysis, how they govern catalytic reaction energetics remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a delta self-consistent field (ΔSCF)-based theoretical framework to investigate catalytic reaction energetics under nonequilibrium electronic conditions and demonstrate it using H2 dissociation, a fundamental hydrogen-activation step, at doped Cu/ZnO photocatalytic interfaces. By constructing and continuously following metastable nonequilibrium electronic configurations along the reaction coordinate, we directly establish their connection with catalytic reaction energetics. We show that illumination-induced catalytic responses are governed not simply by the nonequilibrium electronic configurations accessible under illumination, but by how the resulting electronic perturbations couple to chemically relevant interactions as the reaction proceeds. Depending on catalyst composition, these perturbations give rise to three distinct nonequilibrium response modes, leading to dopant-dependent promotion or inhibition of H2 activation. The present work establishes a mechanistic framework linking evolving nonequilibrium electronic configurations, excitation-induced response modes, and catalytic energetics, providing general design principles for tailoring heterogeneous photocatalysis through nonequilibrium electronic-structure engineering.

Mengru Li, Hao Wang, Hui Yin

item.title: Computational Screening of Functional Nanocluster Precursors for Bottle-around-Ship Encapsulation in Metal-Organic Frameworks
item.description:
Monodisperse, Atomically Precise Nanoclusters (APNCs) exhibit distinct electronic and sizedependent properties, making them uniquely suited for catalysis, sensing, and drug delivery applications. However, their controlled synthesis remains a challenge since the existing methods struggle to reproducibly achieve atomic-level precision in their composition and geometry. Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs), particularly Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks (ZIFs) such as ZIF-8, have emerged as powerful templates for directing APNC synthesis via the bottle-around-ship strategy, in which the MOF framework self-assembles around the pre-formed Nanocluster Precursor (NCP). However, despite considerable experimental progress, no predictive framework exists to determine a priori which NCP-MOF combinations will undergo successful encapsulation and therefore yield well-defined monodisperse APNCs. Here, we develop a computational hierarchical screening workflow that systematically examines the chemical and structural factors that govern successful encapsulation of NCPs. The workflow evaluates four parameters: (i) ground-state spin multiplicity of NCPs, (ii) intrinsic structural stability of isolated NCPs, (iii) spatial compatibility of NCPs within the MOF cavity, and (iv) host-guest interaction energies along with the resulting structural responses in NCP@ZIF-8 composite systems. Applying this workflow to a chemically diverse NCP set spanning Chini-type, Pt-browns, and bimetallic Pt(M) carbonyl clusters, we correctly identify successfully encapsulated precursors. Overall, our strategy offers a cheap transferable route for screening existing and new NCP-MOF combinations.

Poonam, Iñigo Iribarren, Alessio Gagliardi

item.title: Site-selective alkali ion alloying in double perovskites via liquid-assisted mechanosynthesis revealed by solid-state NMR
item.description:
Lead-free halide double perovskites are promising materials for light-emitting and photovoltaic applications. However, compositional tuning of their structural and optoelectronic properties has largely focused on B-site and halide alloying. In this work, we show that Cs + on the perovskite A-site of Cs 2 AgInCl 6 can be partly substituted with Rb + using simple apolar liquid-assisted mechanochemistry. By comparing Rb + with Na + substitution we show that ion size drives the site-selectivity of alkali ion substitution into double perovskites, with Na + preferentially occupying the perovskite B-site. By combining multinuclear solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy with X-ray diffraction, we show that Rb+ not only enters the double-perovskite site-selectively but also induces local symmetry breaking of the cubic structure, comparable to the effect of B-site Na + /Ag + alloying, with important implications for symmetry-forbidden photoluminescence emissivity. This work extends the tuneable compositional range of lead-free double perovskites to include A-site mixing while also establishing the site-selectivity of alkali ion speciation into the double perovskite structure.

Kaja Glazer, Julia Wiktor, Luis Simbari, Mo Al Al Maoued, Anya Fairhurst, Amita Ummadishingu, Dominik J. Kubicki, Benjamin M. Gallant

item.title: Role of ortho-functional groups in stabilizing catechol surface complexes on ferrite nanoparticles
item.description:
Molecular-level interactions of naturally occurring catechol derivatives with ferrite surfaces were investigated using permanently magnetic barium hexaferrite nanoplatelets and superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles. Catechol (1,2-benzenediol) and guaiacol (2-methoxyphenol) were selected as representative aromatic ligands relevant to catechol- and guaiacyl-containing natural compounds. First-principles calculations indicated facile proton transfer from the ligands to surface oxygen or hydroxyl sites and predicted strong H-bonding between the resulting surface-bound species and neighbouring surface groups. Consistent with these predictions, spectroscopic and thermal analyses together with zeta-potential measurements support a surface-complexation mechanism in which the complexes are stabilized by hydrogen bonds, also involving the ortho-phenol or methoxy group and an adjacent surface hydroxyl group. Ligand adsorption did not significantly affect the magnetic behaviour of either ferrite. Both nanoparticle systems remained chemically stable after the catechol adsorption at pH 10, while barium hexaferrite nanoplatelets were also stable under near-neutral conditions. In contrast, catechol derivatives accelerated the decomposition of barium hexaferrite nanoplatelets at pH 3. Moreover, barium hexaferrite nanoplatelets catalyzed the oxidation of catechols by molecular oxygen in aqueous dispersions. These results link proton transfer and hydrogen-bond-assisted surface complexation with the stability of ferrite nanoparticles and reactivity toward catechol ligands in aqueous environments.

Katja Drobež, Matic Poberžnik, Jelena Papan Djaniš, Griša Grogorij Prinčič, Jernej Iskra, Darja Lisjak
